identity.title: Noradrenaline Synergistically Enhances Porphyromonas gingivalis LPS and OMV-Induced Interleukin-1beta Production in BV-2 Microglia Through Differential Mechanisms.

content.abstract: Infection with Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg), which is a major periodontal pathogen, causes a large number of systemic diseases based on chronic inflammation such as diabetes and Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, it is not yet fully understood how Pg can augment local systemic immune and inflammatory responses during progression of AD. There is a strong association between depression and elevated levels of inflammation. Noradrenaline (NA) is a key neurotransmitter that modulates microglial activation during stress conditions. In this study, we have thus investigated the regulatory mechanisms of NA on the production of interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta) by microglia following stimulation with Pg virulence factors, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and outer membrane vesicles (OMVs). NA (30-1000 nM) significantly enhanced the mRNA level, promoter activity, and protein level of IL-1beta up to 20-fold in BV-2 microglia following treatment with Pg LPS (10 mug/mL) and OMVs (150 mug of protein/mL) in a dose-dependent manner. Pharmacological studies have suggested that NA synergistically augments the responses induced by Pg LPS and OMVs through different mechanisms. AP-1 is activated by the beta(2) adrenergic receptor (Abeta(2)R)-mediated pathway. NF-kappaB, which is activated by the Pg LPS/toll-like receptor 2-mediated pathway, is required for the synergistic effect of NA on the Pg LPS-induced IL-1beta production by BV-2 microglia. Co-immunoprecipitation combined with Western blotting and the structural models generated by AlphaFold2 suggested that cross-coupling of NF-kappaB p65 and AP-1 c-Fos transcription factors enhances the binding of NF-kappaB p65 to the IkappaB site, resulting in the synergistic augmentation of the IL-1beta promoter activity. In contrast, OMVs were phagocytosed by BV-2 microglia and then activated the TLR9/p52/RelB-mediated pathway. The Abeta(2)R/Epac-mediated pathway, which promotes phagosome maturation, may be responsible for the synergistic effect of NA on the OMV-induced production of IL-1beta in BV-2 microglia. Our study provides the first evidence that NA synergistically enhances the production of IL-1beta in response to Pg LPS and OMVs through distinct mechanisms.
